subject: Marketplace purchase: coordination, PO path, and MAP for Crestline Systems
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@crestline.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace purchase: MAP & procurement path (AWS private offer?)

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet earlier this week. Attaching a one-page MAP (redwood_map_crestline_v1.pdf) that lays out the sprint from evaluation -> procurement -> go-live for a Marketplace-based private offer. High level asks from our side to keep the timeline tight:

- Confirm procurement contact + preferred PO template (if Procurement prefers vendor-managed or marketplace private offer flow)
- Confirm target go-live date (you mentioned early July)
- Any internal approvals we should plan for (security review, legal redlines, finance signoff)

Proposed next steps (we can compress if you want):
1) Week 0: Finalize MAP and sign mutual action plan doc (this email thread)
2) Week 1: Procurement reviews private-offer draft; finance confirms billing path (marketplace invoice vs direct invoice)
3) Week 2: DocuSign on PO/contract; AWS private offer activation (if chosen)
4) Week 3: Provisioning and a short readiness check, then go-live

If Procurement prefers marketplace private offers, that typically avoids a direct vendor invoice and routes billing through AWS with the private offer terms. If Finance needs a Redwood invoice (direct), we can provide that too — just need to coordinate payment terms.

I attached the MAP and a short procurement checklist to this thread. Laura (cc) will propose the PO language and billing options. Can we schedule a 30-minute procurement sync next week? I’ve left a couple of placeholder times in the calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood_map_crestline_v1.pdf (1p MAP)

Date: Sat, 09 Jun 2028 11:03:22 -0400
Subject: Re: Marketplace purchase: MAP & procurement path (AWS private offer?)

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear MAP. Procurement looped in on this thread (procurement@crestline.com). A few quick answers from our side:

- Target go-live: 2028-07-01 (we're trying to hit product launch)
- Procurement prefers Marketplace Private Offer if possible — it simplifies tax and central billing for us
- Finance will need an estimate for standard monthly run rate and a one-time setup amount for the initial reserved capacity (if applicable)

I’m attaching our PO template for reference (procurement template attached). Can you confirm: 1) whether Redwood can accept the Marketplace Private Offer flow and 2) an expected activation timeline once DocuSign is complete?

Happy to jump on the sync next Tue.

— Sarah
Sarah Miller
Senior PM, Crestline Systems

Subject: Re: Marketplace purchase: MAP & procurement path (AWS private offer?)

Logan / Aditya — quick internal note before our sync with Crestline:

Recommended PO path (based on similar deals):
- Use AWS Marketplace Private Offer (vendor-accepted private offer + marketplace billing)
- Redwood to provide an Offer Acceptance PDF and a short SOW addendum (1 page) for billing/usage bands
- Finance: request standard Net30 on Redwood's side but invoice via AWS billing (marketplace). Crestline Finance can continue normal vendor reconciliation.

Docs we should prepare now:
- AWS private offer draft (attached: aws_private_offer_draft.pdf)
- Procurement checklist for Crestline finance (attached: procurement_checklist_crestline.xlsx)
- Short SOW addendum template (we'll create if Crestline requests)

Notes: if Crestline insists on Redwood invoicing directly (not via Marketplace), we can accommodate but it will add 7-10 business days to billing setup and require a vendor W9/PO flow. Recommend marketplace route to keep timeline.

I included a marked-up draft of the private offer. Aditya, can you confirm the billing code and customer alias we should include for Crestline?

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: aws_private_offer_draft.pdf, procurement_checklist_crestline.xlsx

Hi Sarah / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick response and the PO template. Per Laura’s note, Marketplace Private Offer is the best path to meet your July 1 target. Summary of what I’m sending now:

- AWS private offer draft (aws_private_offer_draft.pdf) attached — this contains pricing bands and the Offer Acceptance language we ask AWS to publish for the private offer
- Estimated monthly run rate: $18k–22k depending on peak usage band (see pricing table in the draft)
- One-time onboarding/setup: $3,500 (covers capacity reservation + integration support)

Action items:
- Procurement: please confirm Crestline's PO reference number and preferred signatory for DocuSign
- Finance: confirm Net30 via AWS marketplace billing or request Redwood direct invoice (will add lead time)
- AWS (cc Mark Davenport): please confirm expected activation SLA for private offers after acceptance (we’ve typically seen 1–3 business days)

I’ll leave a 30-min slot on Tues for the procurement sync (invite sent). If you prefer, we can move to Wed morning.

Thanks —
Logan

Hi all — thanks for the thread. AWS can activate the private offer within 1 business day after the Offer Acceptance is published and both buyer/seller have confirmed the marketplace terms. From AWS side we need:

- Seller acceptance confirmation (Logan / Redwood)
- Buyer acceptance (procurement@crestline.com)
- The signed Offer Acceptance PDF or DocuSign link (we can pull the acceptance once it’s live)

Proposed timeline based on current cadence:
- 6/13: Crestline procurement sends signed PO / DocuSign (assuming sync goes well)
- 6/14: Redwood to publish Offer Acceptance; AWS activates private offer within 1 business day
- 6/14–6/15: Billing mapping and account alias verified (Redwood to confirm alias)
- 6/15–6/18: Provisioning and readiness; target go-live 6/25 if Crestline wants an earlier ramp; otherwise 7/1 per their launch date

If Crestline confirms market place flow, that preserves your tax and consolidated billing. If you need Redwood invoicing directly instead, let me know and we’ll note that in the activation checklist (longer lead time).

— Mark Davenport
AWS Marketplace Seller Support
mark.davenport@amazon.com
